title: ACs get an opportunity to respond but are explicitly denied the benefit of the doubt
content:
A.1.5.9 makes the Core Facilitator responsible for adjudicating formal allegations against ACs and mandates holding them "to the highest standard of Universal Alignment, without granting them the benefit of the doubt." A.1.5.9.1 then requires that the accused be given "an opportunity to respond," and its Action Tenet A.1.5.9.1.0.4.1 specifies content: "sufficient time to prepare a response, the ability to submit information or evidence, and reasonable access to any information pertinent to the allegation." Whistleblower identities stay confidential.

These two provisions are usually bundled together as "due process," and separating them is instructive. What the accused receives is **participation**: notice, time, the ability to put evidence in, and sight of the case. What they do not receive is a **presumption**: ambiguity is resolved against them, consistent with the 51% derecognition threshold in A.1.5.4.0.4.1 and its bar on excusing "ignorance of the rules, good intentions, honest mistake."

The rationale is that the two serve different purposes. Participation improves the accuracy of the finding — it surfaces facts the adjudicator lacks, as the resignation-email scenario (A.1.5.5.0.4.1.1.3) shows, where the entity's own evidence produced an Aligned finding. A presumption of innocence, by contrast, allocates the cost of uncertainty, and the Atlas has decided that cost falls on the individual rather than the ecosystem.

NR-5 puts the question openly rather than letting it sit implied: "Specific logic currently active in the Atlas clearly indicates that ACs are held to the highest standards of Universal Alignment. Such a standard would seem to indicate that 'fairness' is not an objective in any proceeding involving AC derecognition. What are the arguments for and against this?" Whether procedural participation without a favourable presumption is coherent as a system, rather than merely functional, is left unresolved by the framework itself.
description: A.1.5.9 mandates the highest standard 'without granting them the benefit of the doubt', while A.1.5.9.1 guarantees time, evidence submission and access — procedure without a presumption of innocence.
